newsitem.title: USA: Mother guilty of murder of boy adopted from Russia.
newsitem.headline: Mother guilty of murder of boy adopted from Russia.

text.p: A woman who claimed the boy she adopted from a Russian orphanage suffered from a psychological disorder that led to his death was found guilty on Tuesday of his murder.
A jury of eight women and four men found Renee Polreis, 44, guilty of child abuse resulting in the death of her 2-year-old son David.
She faced from 16 to 48 years in prison, prosecutor Al Dominguez said. The jury deliberated a little under two hours.
"It was a very difficult case because of the subject matter. All of our expert witnesses indicated it was one of the worst cases (of child abuse) they have ever seen," Dominguez told Reuters.

The case drew national attention because defence attorneys claimed that the boy, who was adopted from a Russian orphanage in 1995, six months before he died in February 1996, suffered from reactive attachment disorder and had a history of self-mutilation.
The disorder, which often stems from a newborn not receiving sufficient affection, prevented him from creating a bond with his mother and also caused him to fly into rages, the defence team said.
They argued the boy's injuries were either self-inflicted, which triggered a lung infection, or caused by emergency medical technicians when they were summoned to the home.

Prosecutors said the woman beat the child, and expert witnesses testified that the boy received a terrible beating the day he died. Police found two broken wooden spoons wrapped in a bloody diaper in the garbage the day the boy was taken to the hospital.
One witness testified that Polreis described the child's behaviour as so difficult that she wanted to end the adoption, but that her husband insisted on keeping the child.
Damaging testimony came from a psychotherapist who said Polreis called him before she contacted police, saying she had hurt the child.
The couple has another adopted son.
